new_page.title: BC Home Flipping Tax: 20% on Sales Within 2 Years (2026 Guide)
new_page.h1: What is the BC home flipping tax?
new_page.description: Sell a BC home or presale contract within two years and the home flipping tax may apply: 20% of the profit inside 365 days, falling to zero at 730 days.

breadcrumbs.name: What is the BC home flipping tax?

faq.q: Does the BC flipping tax apply if I owned the home for over two years?
faq.a: No. It applies only when you owned it for less than 730 days.

faq.q: Does it apply to presale assignments?
faq.a: Yes. A presale contract is a right to acquire residential property, so assigning it within 730 days of signing can be taxed.

parts.t: Since January 1, 2025, BC taxes the profit when you sell a home, or assign a presale contract, that you owned for less than 730 days. The rate is 20% of the profit if you sell within 365 days, then it falls gradually to zero at 730 days. It is a separate return, usually due within 90 days of the sale.
Residential property in BC, and the right to buy it, which includes presale contracts. The clock runs from the day you acquired it to the day you sell or assign it.

blocks.text: Exemptions and the principal residence deduction

parts.t: Some life events can exempt a sale, and some exemptions need a return to be filed. If the home was your principal residence and you owned it at least 365 days in a row, up to $20,000 of the profit can be deducted. That deduction is not available when you assign a presale.

The flipping tax return is separate from your income tax return. If the tax applies, or an exemption needs a return, you generally file within 90 days of the sale. The federal anti-flipping rule (profit taxed as business income if you sell within 365 days) is separate and can apply as well.

If you might sell within two years, for a move, a presale assignment or a renovation project, plan the dates with your accountant before you buy. Selling on day 731 instead of day 700 can change the bill.
Read on November 18, 2026. Rules change, so confirm with the source or your lawyer, notary or accountant before you act.
